findings.highlight: Sakura and Tohsaka are a good Senpai and junior, and Fuji-nee is completely friends with Tohsaka now.
findings.evidenceJa: 桜と遠坂はいい先輩と後輩だし、藤ねえも今ではすっかり遠坂の味方だし
findings.governingReading: Sakura and Rin have a good senior-junior relationship, and Taiga is now thoroughly on Rin’s side.
findings.explanation: The English is grammatically malformed and changes Taiga’s alignment with Rin into generic friendship.

findings.highlight: there’s something wrong with all of us eating right now
findings.evidenceJa: こうしてみんなで飯を食っていると
findings.governingReading: As everyone eats together like this, Shirou feels that something is wrong.
findings.explanation: The English drops the relational force of eating together and substitutes mere simultaneity.

findings.highlight: I grab Saber’s hand and take her to the living room.
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーの手を強引に引っ張ったまま居間についた
findings.governingReading: Still forcefully pulling the hand he took earlier, Shirou reaches the living room with Saber.
findings.explanation: The English repeats the hand-grab as a new action and loses the continuity of his impulsive physical insistence.

findings.evidenceJa: あなた、何の為にここに来たのよ
findings.governingReading: Taiga directly asks Saber why she came; the active Japanese supplies no following gaze sentence.
findings.explanation: The English conditionally restores a commented-out glare, adding hostility absent from the active witness.

findings.evidenceJa: 風雲急を告げるような効果音を背負って
findings.governingReading: Accompanied by sound effects heralding a sudden dramatic crisis, Taiga leads everyone outside.
findings.explanation: The English reads the idiom as literal wind and loses the narrator’s mock-dramatic framing.

findings.highlight: what is the purpose of this?
findings.evidenceJa: それはどういった理屈でしょうか
findings.governingReading: Saber asks what sort of logic supports Taiga’s proposed test.
findings.explanation: The English asks for its purpose instead, weakening Saber’s challenge to Taiga’s reasoning.

findings.highlight: I can entrust Shirou to you just for a bit.
findings.evidenceJa: それなら少しは士郎を任せてもいいわよーだ
findings.governingReading: If Saber is stronger, Taiga will concede that she can entrust Shirou to her at least to some degree.
findings.explanation: The English changes limited confidence into a short duration.

findings.highlight: Fuji-nee’s clever attack to the body strikes
findings.evidenceJa: そこに炸裂する、藤ねえの小手先胴
findings.governingReading: Taiga’s distinctive 小手先胴 striking phrase erupts against the motionless Saber.
findings.explanation: The English parses 小手先 as “clever” and normalizes the marked kendo wording into a generic body attack.

findings.evidenceJa: ヘンなのに士郎とられちゃった
findings.governingReading: Taiga wails that some weirdo has taken Shirou from her.
findings.explanation: “Stranger” removes the childish insult that completes her comic emotional reversal.

findings.highlight: Fuji-nee said “I want to talk a bit” and went into Father’s room for two hours.
findings.evidenceJa: 藤ねえが「ちょっとだけ話がしたい」とセイバーと親父の部屋に閉じこもって二時間が経ち
findings.governingReading: Taiga shuts herself in Kiritsugu’s room with Saber and talks for two hours.
findings.explanation: The English omits Saber from the private conversation, obscuring who persuades Taiga and how recognition is reached.

findings.highlight: No reason. I just introduced you because I didn’t like it.
findings.evidenceJa: 単に嫌だったから紹介しただけだ
findings.governingReading: Shirou says there is no elaborate “why”: he introduced Saber simply because he hated leaving her out.
findings.explanation: “No reason” contradicts the motive immediately stated and makes his answer sound incoherent.

findings.evidenceJa: 星座がはっきりと見渡せた
findings.governingReading: The winter sky is high, with the constellations distinctly visible across it.
findings.explanation: The English generalizes constellations into stars and drops the expansive visual field.

findings.highlight: It’s only natural for Tohsaka to be disgusted with me.
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂に呆れられるのも当然だ
findings.governingReading: Shirou thinks it natural that Rin would be exasperated or appalled by his contradiction.
findings.explanation: “Disgusted” intensifies Rin’s reaction into moral revulsion and distorts their relationship tone.

findings.highlight: I thought I was only inexperienced at magic
findings.evidenceJa: 未熟なのは魔術だけだと思ってたけど
findings.governingReading: Shirou had thought his immaturity was limited to magecraft.
findings.explanation: The English again collapses 魔術 into undifferentiated “magic.”

findings.evidenceJa: 小さな自分を積んでいく事しか出来なかった
findings.governingReading: All Shirou can do is keep piling up his small, immature self, believing accumulated effort may someday reach something.
findings.explanation: “Refine myself” removes the concrete accumulation image and smooths away the coexistence of effort and self-diminishment.
